items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: And Bob Prince didn’t know it, so he asked Coleman to sing it to him.

ctx.x: Yeah. George Avakian put that together on the spur of the moment. And also there is a very obscure album which should be reissued. Warner Brothers is doing some jazz in the late 50s or early 60s, and there was this guy named Bob Prince, an arranger, and he did these two oddball albums. One was — I think it was twelve trombones or something, it was all trombones. Then there’s one that’s called Saxophones Incorporated, and it was twelve saxophones I think. And it sounded like a big band. You didn’t even miss the…
No, I just wanted to see if you remembered it, and if it was a good date for you.
